quote: This is calling with Ion. I got a request to look at a disclaimer for your line. How are you interested? Have a veteran discount and you have Tesla
stewart_read: The rep never states their own name clearly and the phrase 'disclaimer for your line' does not map to any coherent lead-source explanation, leaving legitimacy unestablished at the open.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a transcription/diarization artifact (Deepgram garbling), not necessarily a rep failure — the audio may have been clearer.
coaching_implication: Even accounting for possible transcription noise, the manager should confirm the rep is running a clean, complete intro template naming themselves and the lead source (Tesla referral) in the first 10 seconds.

stewart_read: A $400/month bill was captured cleanly as a strong pain point, but the rep's reaction ('Oh my goodness. 400. Okay. Yeah. We'll definitely help you get that cut down.') acknowledges but does not flip it into alignment-against-the-utility before moving straight to the credit qualifier.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pause on high bill figures and use them as leverage ('that's money going to the utility instead of your own system') before moving to the next qualifier.

quote: I'm a retired disabled veteran and retired Connecticut state employee. So my money is only a certain amount, and I don't know what my credit is doing right now.
stewart_read: The customer disclosed veteran status, retirement, and fixed income as a vulnerability/trust gift. The rep's only response is 'Mhmm. Okay.' before pivoting straight into the disqualifying credit advice, with no acknowledgment of the disclosure itself.
coaching_implication: Model an acknowledgment ('I appreciate your service, and I hear you on the fixed income') before delivering any qualifying news — this is the trust-gift moment the schema flags as costing more than any single procedural gap when skipped.

quote: Well, yeah, if I were you, Irvin, I would wait to look into solar until you know that your credit is above $6.70.
stewart_read: The rep unilaterally disqualifies on a customer's stated 'I have no idea' about credit rather than passing the lead through to a closer/credit pull. Per the schema's spencer_operator_note, stated credit is unreliable and DQ'ing on 'I don't know' (not even a stated low number) is a policy question that should default to letting the closer decide, not the setter killing the lead outright.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep followed a hard rule as trained, believing DQ-on-unknown is correct procedure. Strategic read is not supported — there is no evidence the rep planned a follow-up or alternate path; the call simply ends.
coaching_implication: This is the single highest-leverage moment on the call. The manager should clarify with Kenny whether setters should ever self-DQ on 'I don't know my credit' versus booking anyway and flagging for the closer's actual credit pull.

quote: Just that Alright. Thank you for everything. Have a great day. Please remove me from your list.
stewart_read: The call ends with the customer requesting removal from the call list — a direct, measurable consequence of the prior line. There is no recovery attempt, no offer to proceed contingent on a credit check, and no button-up of any kind.
coaching_implication: Show the rep the direct causal link between the DQ-on-stated-unknown line and the customer's immediate request to be removed — this is the clearest before/after in the call for illustrating the cost of that call's ending.

quote: And it looks like a pretty decent home for solar. You have a really good southern exposure, which is exactly what you look for.
stewart_read: The rep identifies a genuinely qualifying positive attribute (southern exposure) early in the call — a good practice that built momentum before the ending collapsed it.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this behavior — noting positive home attributes builds customer confidence early. Worth pointing out as something the rep did well before the credit-handling misstep.

quote: for any other programs and state incentives that you can qualify for, you just need to have a credit score above 670. Is that the case for you?
stewart_read: The customer's fixed-income/veteran disclosure directly maps to the objection-inversion pattern — his financial constraint is exactly the situation solar's savings would help, but the rep treats it purely as a disqualifying data point rather than reframing ("your fixed income is exactly why cutting that $400 bill matters").
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep is following a rigid hard-DQ rule as trained rather than choosing not to flip; there's no evidence of a deliberate strategic choice here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on using the stated financial constraint as leverage for urgency rather than as an automatic exit ramp.
